_about: The 10 classification precedence rules, plus cross-topic policy. Rules are evaluated IN ORDER; the first whose signals all fire wins and supplies primary_category. Every record records which rule fired and why.
_cross_topic_about: Duplicate suppression WITHIN one topic is mandatory and not configurable: one record per identity_url per topic. Behaviour ACROSS topics is this setting, because global cross-topic suppression was never an approved requirement and a genuine multi-topic classification must not be silently discarded.

_cross_topic_options.cross_reference: Owning topic (highest precedence rank) emits a full record; every other qualifying topic emits a cross_reference row pointing at it. Not an independent duplicate, and not discarded.
_cross_topic_options.multi_publish: Every qualifying topic emits a full record carrying multi_topic[] and multi_topic_reason.
_cross_topic_options.suppress: Non-owning topics emit nothing. The run manifest still records the suppression and its reason.
_cross_topic_options.link: Full records everywhere, joined only by content_id, with no ownership designation.

_rank_about: Topic ownership rank when the same content qualifies under more than one topic. Lower number wins. Derived from how specific the topic's claim on a piece of content is.
_rules_about: Signals are computed by src/harvest/classify.py from title, summary, publisher, target_url and the source's own category. `all_of` must every fire; `none_of` must none fire. `assign` names the winning category by slug.

rules.description: A concrete organization-level implementation with measurable results belongs in Case Studies.
A generally applicable industry solution or adoption pattern belongs in Domain Applications.
A standalone end-user or business solution belongs in Product Discovery. Developer-productivity tools are excluded and are never reclassified into this category.
A model release, model version, API, pricing or protocol change belongs in Model Updates, NOT Big Tech Trends.
Funding, investment, acquisition or financial activity belongs in Market & Investment, NOT Big Tech Trends.
New evaluation resources, datasets, leaderboards or benchmark results belong in Benchmark & Datasets, EVEN WHEN associated with a paper.
A primary academic contribution belongs in Papers.
Engineering implementation analysis belongs in Technical Deep Dives.
Argumentative, predictive or thesis-driven commentary belongs in Insights & Opinions.
When ambiguity remains, fall back to the cell the candidate was discovered in, and record every competing category plus the rationale in audit metadata. Exactly one primary_category is still chosen.

_signal_about: Signals are keyword/structure predicates over the candidate. Deterministic and auditable — no model call. Each fired signal contributes its matched evidence to classification.evidence[].
_matching_about: any_of_keywords matches WHOLE CASEFOLDED TOKENS, never an arbitrary substring: term and text are tokenized identically (maximal runs of word characters), so 'ide' matches 'IDE' but not 'guide', and 'product' matches 'product' but not 'production'. A multi-token term must match a contiguous run of complete tokens, respecting boundaries at both ends. A term ending in '*' is an explicit token-prefix stem constraining only its final token — 'deprecat*' matches deprecate/deprecated/deprecation and still cannot begin inside another token. any_of_patterns are regexes matched CASE-SENSITIVELY against the raw field, because they use [A-Z] to mean a proper noun.
_language_scope_about: Keyword terms are English only, and every configured source is an English-language feed. Token matching needs word separators, so a term in a script that does not use them (Japanese, Chinese) cannot work here without script-aware segmentation this pipeline deliberately does not have. A lone Japanese term carried in is_funding_or_ma_event since 0edbf50 was removed in S4-3A rather than left as an inert claim of multilingual coverage. Adding a non-English term requires a segmentation contract first.
